hints: Focus on what makes an ester an ester, the $\text{-COO-}$ group in the middle with a carbon chain on each side.
Split the 4 total carbons between the acid side ($\text{RCOO-}$) and the alcohol side ($\text{-R'}$), remembering the $\text{COO}$ carbon counts as one.
Systematically work through 3-carbon acid plus 1-carbon alcohol, 2 plus 2, then 1 plus 3, and check if the 3-carbon side can branch.
walkthrough:
**Recall the ester pattern**

Think of every ester as $\text{R-C(=O)-O-R'}$. The $\text{C(=O)O}$ part uses up 1 carbon and both oxygens, so the R and R' groups must share the other 3 carbons.

General ester:
$$\text{R-C(=O)-O-R'}$$

**Split the carbons systematically**

Let acid part = carbons in $\text{R}$ + 1 for $\text{C=O}$. Let alcohol part = carbons in $\text{R'}$. Total must be 4. So try 3+1, 2+2, and 1+3.

$$\text{acid C + alcohol C = 4}$$

**Draw the four combinations**

1. 3-carbon acid + 1-carbon alcohol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$, methyl propanoate. 2. 2-carbon acid + 2-carbon alcohol: $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, ethyl ethanoate. 3. 1-carbon acid + 3-carbon alcohol, straight chain: $\text{HCOOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, propyl methanoate. 4. 1-carbon acid + 3-carbon alcohol, branched: $\text{HCOOCH(CH}_3)_2$, 1-methylethyl methanoate.

$$\text{4 distinct esters in total}$$

options.A: 2 is too few. This usually comes from counting only ethyl ethanoate and methyl propanoate and forgetting the two methanoate esters made from methanoic acid.
options.B: 3 misses one isomer. Most students who pick this count the first three straight-chain esters but forget that the propyl group in propyl methanoate can be branched to give 1-methylethyl methanoate.
options.C: 4 is correct. The complete set is methyl propanoate, ethyl ethanoate, propyl methanoate and 1-methylethyl methanoate. No other splitting of 4 carbons around the $\text{-COO-}$ group is possible.
options.D: 5 is one too many. This trap comes from counting a carboxylic acid isomer like butanoic acid or an extra non-ester, but the question asks for esters only, and there are just 4.
